candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'Be hopeful, ye righteous; for suddenly shall the sinners perish before you, and ye shall have lordship over them according to your desires' — the hope-oracle counterpart to the woe oracles. Tewahedo hope-theology (persecution-resilience preserved through Aksum-era persecutions, Gragn invasion, the Derg-era massacres of monks) draws on this Enochic hope-formula: present suffering does not falsify the eschatological reversal.
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition), Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108). Verify the summary still reflects the source's argument before promoting; substitute a verbatim quote from the NPNF / Charles dump where available, and where applicable cross-check the Andəmta homiletic tradition for resonance.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'Be hopeful, therefore, ye who have suffered tribulation; for ye shall have great joy as the angels of heaven' — equal-to-the-angels promise. Tewahedo monastic spirituality reads this verse as the canonical anchor for the doctrine that the eschatological state of the saints is angelic-in-rank — parallel to Lk 20:35-36 ('equal unto the angels') and 1 Cor 15:48-49.
